steps.say: Truncus arteriosus breaks the most basic rule of heart plumbing. A single common arterial trunk is arising from the heart and feeding the body, the lungs, and the coronary arteries all at once. A large ventricular septal defect is always lying beneath it, so oxygen rich and oxygen poor blood are mixing completely before distribution.
steps.tx: **Persistent truncus arteriosus** features a single **common arterial trunk** arising from the heart that supplies the **systemic, pulmonary, and coronary circulations** together. A large malalignment ventricular septal defect always lies beneath the trunk, mixing lets the lungs flood under systemic pressure, and heart failure with mild cyanosis declares itself within days of birth.

vis.alt: Persistent truncus arteriosus diagram showing a single common trunk overriding a malalignment ventricular septal defect, a truncal valve and pulmonary arteries arising from the trunk
vis.caption: Persistent truncus arteriosus diagram showing a single common trunk overriding a malalignment ventricular septal defect, a truncal valve and pulmonary arteries arising from the trunk. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: The single valve guarding this common trunk is rarely normal. It carries between one and six cusps, most often three or four, and it is frequently thickened and dysplastic. About a fifth to a third of patients have meaningful leakage through it, which dramatically raises the stakes of surgical repair.
steps.tx: The **truncal valve morphology** is dysplastic, with **1 to 6 cusps**, most commonly tricuspid or quadricuspid, and exhibits insufficiency in **20-30%** of patients. A severely leaking truncal valve floods the ventricle in diastole and worsens the already torrential pulmonary overcirculation, so its severity decides whether valve surgery joins the neonatal repair.

points: Three thin cusps opening fully in systole
Competent closure with no diastolic leak
Repair focuses on the VSD and lung flow
left.title: Competent Truncal Valve

points: One to six thick dysplastic cusps, often four
Valvuloplasty or replacement joins the repair
right.title: Regurgitant Truncal Valve

steps.say: Surgeons classify truncus by where the lung arteries take off. In Collett and Edwards type I a short pulmonary trunk rises and splits, in type II the two arteries leave the back of the trunk close together, and in type III they exit from the sides. Knowing the pattern tells the surgeon where to harvest and reconnect the pulmonary arteries.
steps.tx: **Collett and Edwards classification** maps pulmonary artery origin: **Type I** has a short **pulmonary trunk** branching into left and right arteries; **Type II** has separate arteries arising close together from the **dorsal truncus**; **Type III** has arteries arising from the **lateral sides**. The pattern dictates how the surgeon detaches the arteries and rebuilds them onto the new right ventricular outflow.

steps.say: One variant bundles truncus with a broken aortic arch. Van Praagh type A4 adds coarctation or an interrupted arch with a large patent ductus feeding the lower body. These babies need prostaglandin to keep the duct open until the arch is rebuilt alongside the truncus repair.
steps.tx: The **Van Praagh classification** labels this lesion **type A4**, which incorporates **coarctation or interrupted aortic arch** with a large **patent ductus arteriosus** supplying descending aortic flow. The arch obstruction adds a second pressure load and a duct dependent lower body, so prostaglandin infusion bridges the baby to a single stage repair that fixes the trunk, the septal defect, and the arch together.

nodes.label: Common trunk supplies the upper body while the arch is interrupted below
Large patent ductus carries trunk blood down to the descending aorta
Prostaglandin keeps the duct open until the operation begins
Single stage repair rebuilds the arch, closes the VSD and restores lung flow

steps.say: Truncus arteriosus should always prompt a look at chromosome 22. More than a third of cases carry the chromosome 22 deletion of DiGeorge syndrome. That means checking calcium, T cell counts, and the palate alongside the heart, because immune and airway problems shape recovery after surgery.
steps.tx: **DiGeorge syndrome association** is strong: over **30-40%** of truncus cases carry the **chromosome 22q11.2 microdeletion**. Affected babies may add hypocalcaemia, T cell deficiency, cleft palate, and learning difficulty to their cardiac disease, so fluorescence testing, calcium monitoring, and irradiated blood products become part of the perioperative plan.

points: Hypocalcaemia with T cell immune deficiency
Needs irradiated blood and calcium watch
left.title: Truncus with DiGeorge

steps.say: Truncus cannot wait. Flooding lungs develop irreversible vascular disease within weeks, so complete repair happens in the first month of life. The surgeon patches the septal defect to commit the left ventricle to the trunk and connects the right ventricle to the lung arteries with a valved homograft conduit.
steps.tx: **Early surgical repair** within **1 month** of birth prevents irreversible pulmonary vascular disease from systemic pressure lung flow. A patch closes the **VSD** to commit the left ventricle to the truncus as the new aorta, while an **RV to PA valved homograft conduit** restores a separate pulmonary outflow, with duct ligation and arch repair added when needed.

vis.alt: Heart diagram showing a secundum atrial septal defect, a membranous ventricular septal defect, right ventricular outflow obstruction and an overriding aorta.
vis.caption: Septal defect with overriding great vessel committed to the left ventricle at repair. Illustration: StewardMD.

steps.say: A leaking truncal valve cannot be left behind at the repair. Significant regurgitation forces the surgeon to reshape the valve with a valvuloplasty or replace it outright during the same neonatal operation. Ignoring it leaves the baby in low output failure no matter how perfect the rest of the repair.
steps.tx: **Truncal regurgitation severity** decides the operation: significant leakage requires concomitant **truncal valvuloplasty or replacement** during neonatal repair. Cusp repair techniques thin and resuspend the dysplastic leaflets, replacement is reserved for unrepairable valves, and either choice raises operative risk well above that of truncus repair with a competent valve.

rows: May need valve work in childhood

steps.say: The bedside diagnosis of truncus is made through the pulses. Massive runoff from the trunk into the low resistance lung arteries during diastole drops the diastolic pressure and produces bounding pulses with a wide pulse pressure. An ejection murmur, a single loud second sound, and early heart failure are firming up the diagnosis before the scan.
steps.tx: **Bounding pulses in truncus** come from massive diastolic **runoff** from the common trunk into low resistance **pulmonary arteries**, producing a **wide pulse pressure** with low diastolic readings. The full bedside picture adds a systolic ejection murmur, a single accentuated second sound from one semilunar valve, tachypnoea with poor feeds, and mild cyanosis from complete mixing.

nodes.label: Common trunk feeds low resistance pulmonary arteries in diastole
Diastolic runoff drops aortic diastolic pressure while systole stays high
Wide pulse pressure with bounding pulses marks the bedside diagnosis
